test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which country is not the part of proposed TAPI gas pipeline?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The name TAPI stands for the four countries involved: **Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India.**
 
• The TAPI pipeline aims to transport natural gas from Turkmenistan to India,** passing through Afghanistan and Pakistan.** 
 
• The idea for the TAPI pipeline was** first proposed in 1990.** The project was **officially launched in 2002.**
 
• The pipeline will transport natural gas from the **Galkynysh gas field in Turkmenistan**, one of the largest gas fields in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Turkmenistan**

 
 
• **Location**: Central Asia, bordered by the Caspian Sea to the west, Kazakhstan to the northwest, Uzbekistan to the northeast, Afghanistan to the southeast, and Iran to the south.
 
• **Capital**: Ashgabat.
 
• **Official Language**: Turkmen.
 
• **Government**: Turkmenistan is a presidential republic. The President holds significant power and authority.
 
 
 
• **Iran**
 
 
• **Location**: Western Asia, bordered by the Caspian Sea to the north, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan to the northeast, Pakistan to the southeast, and several countries to the west (including Iraq and Turkey).
 
• **Capital**: Tehran.
 
• **Official Language**: Persian (Farsi).
 
• **Government**: An Islamic Republic with a Supreme Leader holding significant power alongside an elected President.
 
 
 
• **Afghanistan**
 
 
• **Location**: South Asia and Central Asia, bordered by Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan to the north, Iran to the west, and Pakistan to the east and south.
 
• **Capital**: Kabul.
 
• **Official Languages**: Dari and Pashto.
 
• **Government**: Afghanistan has experienced various forms of governance, currently operating under the Taliban regime since 2021.
